instruction.text: Build a 🚗 AI Vision Smart Boom Barrier Gate circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: Computer vision-driven automated parking boom barrier! The webcam AI pipeline detects approaching vehicles in real-time. When a 'car' class is recognized with high confidence, the Arduino Uno pulses PWM pin D6 to swing the servo gate arm up to 90°, illuminates the Green pass indicator on D12 (turning off Red D13), and logs telemetry to Serial. When the path clears, the barrier smoothly lowers back to 0° with Red stop illuminated.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">9600</field><next>
      <block type="servo_write"><field name="PIN">6</field><value name="ANGLE"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">0</field></shadow></value></block>
      </next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0">
          <block type="ai_is_detected"><field name="CLASS">car</field></block>
        </value>
        <statement name="DO0">
          <block type="serial_println"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">🚗 [AI Vision] Car Detected! Raising Boom Barrier...</field></block></value><next>
          <block type="servo_write"><field name="PIN">6</field><value name="ANGLE"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">90</field></shadow></value><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">12</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">800</field></shadow></value></block>
          </next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block>
        </statement>
        <statement name="ELSE">
          <block type="servo_write"><field name="PIN">6</field><value name="ANGLE"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">0</field></shadow></value><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">12</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">300</field></shadow></value></block>
          </next></block></next></block></next></block>
        </statement>
      </block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a 📱 ESP32 Smart Home Web Server & Phone Controller circuit using ESP32.

target.explanation: Embedded IoT web server with wireless smartphone home automation! The ESP32 connects to Virtual Wi-Fi (SSID: SmartHome-WiFi), establishes an HTTP server on port 80, and serves an interactive web dashboard. Receiving client requests on endpoints /red/on, /red/off, /blue/on, or /blue/off triggers digital GPIO pins D4 and D15 to switch physical Living Room and Bedroom LEDs in real-time, responding with synchronized HTML status badges.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">115200</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">4</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">15</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="wifi_connect">
        <value name="SSID"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">SmartHome-WiFi</field></block></value>
        <value name="PASS"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">pixiu123</field></block></value>
        <next>
        <block type="wifi_server_begin">
          <field name="PORT">80</field>
          <next>
          <block type="wifi_server_on">
            <field name="PATH">/</field>
            <statement name="DO">
              <block type="wifi_server_send">
                <field name="STATUS">200</field>
                <field name="TYPE">text/html</field>
                <value name="CONTENT">
                  <block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT"><h1>🏠 ESP32 Smart Home</h1><p>Tap to control room lights:</p><div><a href="/red/on">Turn ON Living Room</a><a href="/red/off">Turn OFF Living Room</a></div><div style="margin-top:10px;"><a href="/blue/on">Turn ON Bedroom</a><a href="/blue/off">Turn OFF Bedroom</a></div></field></block>
                </value>
              </block>
            </statement>
            <next>
            <block type="wifi_server_on">
              <field name="PATH">/red/on</field>
              <statement name="DO">
                <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">4</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
                <block type="wifi_server_send">
                  <field name="STATUS">200</field>
                  <field name="TYPE">text/html</field>
                  <value name="CONTENT">
                    <block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT"><h2 style="color:#ef4444">🔴 Living Room Light: ON</h2><a href="/">← Back to Dashboard</a></field></block>
                  </value>
                </block>
                </next></block>
              </statement>
              <next>
              <block type="wifi_server_on">
                <field name="PATH">/red/off</field>
                <statement name="DO">
                  <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">4</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
                  <block type="wifi_server_send">
                    <field name="STATUS">200</field>
                    <field name="TYPE">text/html</field>
                    <value name="CONTENT">
                      <block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT"><h2>⚪ Living Room Light: OFF</h2><a href="/">← Back to Dashboard</a></field></block>
                    </value>
                  </block>
                  </next></block>
                </statement>
                <next>
                <block type="wifi_server_on">
                  <field name="PATH">/blue/on</field>
                  <statement name="DO">
                    <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">15</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
                    <block type="wifi_server_send">
                      <field name="STATUS">200</field>
                      <field name="TYPE">text/html</field>
                      <value name="CONTENT">
                        <block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT"><h2 style="color:#38bdf8">🔵 Bedroom Light: ON</h2><a href="/">← Back to Dashboard</a></field></block>
                      </value>
                    </block>
                    </next></block>
                  </statement>
                  <next>
                  <block type="wifi_server_on">
                    <field name="PATH">/blue/off</field>
                    <statement name="DO">
                      <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">15</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
                      <block type="wifi_server_send">
                        <field name="STATUS">200</field>
                        <field name="TYPE">text/html</field>
                        <value name="CONTENT">
                          <block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT"><h2>⚪ Bedroom Light: OFF</h2><a href="/">← Back to Dashboard</a></field></block>
                        </value>
                      </block>
                      </next></block>
                    </statement>
                  </block>
                  </next></block>
                </next></block>
              </next></block>
            </next></block>
          </block>
          </next></block>
        </next></block>
      </next></block></next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">100</field></shadow></value></block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a 🕹️ Raspberry Pi Pico Retro OLED Arcade Console circuit using Raspberry Pi Pico.

target.explanation: Retro handheld gaming console built on the RP2040 Raspberry Pi Pico! The system initializes a 128×64 SSD1306 OLED over I2C (GP4 SDA / GP5 SCL) displaying game scores. Polling tactile button GP14 detects player fire inputs, instantly updating the OLED with a laser animation, strobing the green blaster LED on GP16, and emitting high-frequency pulse-width audio on GP15 buzzer.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">115200</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">14</field><field name="MODE">INPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">15</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">16</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="oled_print"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">🎮 PICO ARCADE</field></block></value></block>
      </next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0">
          <block type="io_digitalread"><field name="PIN">14</field></block>

instruction.text: Build a ⛅ ESP32 IoT Weather Station & Smartphone Telemetry circuit using ESP32.

target.explanation: Cloud-connected microclimate monitoring station! The ESP32 samples digital temperature and humidity data from DHT11 on GPIO 4 and analog ambient sunlight from an LDR on GPIO 34. Connecting over Virtual Wi-Fi, it hosts a real-time web portal on port 80 that formats and streams live environmental telemetry directly to simulated smartphones, while pulsing the green telemetry TX activity LED on GPIO 2 each time data packets are dispatched.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">115200</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">2</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="wifi_connect">
        <value name="SSID"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">SmartHome-WiFi</field></block></value>
        <value name="PASS"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">pixiu123</field></block></value>
        <next>
        <block type="wifi_server_begin">
          <field name="PORT">80</field>
          <next>
          <block type="wifi_server_on">
            <field name="PATH">/</field>
            <statement name="DO">
              <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">2</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
              <block type="wifi_server_send">
                <field name="STATUS">200</field>
                <field name="TYPE">text/html</field>
                <value name="CONTENT">
                  <block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT"><h1>⛅ ESP32 Cloud Weather</h1><div style="background:#0f172a;padding:12px;border-radius:8px;"><h3 style="color:#38bdf8;">🌡️ Temperature: {{TEMP}}°C</h3><h3 style="color:#22c55e;">💧 Humidity: {{HUMIDITY}}%</h3><h3 style="color:#eab308;">☀️ Ambient Light: {{LUX}} Lux</h3></div><p style="color:#94a3b8;">Live Virtual Wi-Fi telemetry stream active.</p></field></block>
                </value>
                <next>
                <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">150</field></shadow></value><next>
                <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">2</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field></block>
                </next></block>
                </next>
              </block>
              </next></block>
            </statement>
          </block>
          </next></block>
        </next></block>
      </next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">100</field></shadow></value></block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

The Arduino sweeps a servo turret on D9 between 45° and 135° while firing 40kHz ultrasonic sound pulses from HC-SR04 (Trig D10, Echo D11). Detecting an object closer than 25cm triggers emergency Red LED D12 and rapid buzzer pulses on D8. Clear paths revert to Yellow warning (D7) or safe Green illumination (D6).
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">9600</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">12</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">7</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">6</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field></block>
      </next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="servo_write"><field name="PIN">9</field><value name="ANGLE"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">45</field></shadow></value><next>
      <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">300</field></shadow></value><next>
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0">
          <block type="logic_compare"><field name="OP">LT</field>
            <value name="A"><block type="ultrasonic_read"><field name="TRIG">10</field><field name="ECHO">11</field></block></value>
            <value name="B"><block type="math_number"><field name="NUM">25</field></block></value>
          </block>
        </value>
        <statement name="DO0">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">12</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">7</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">6</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">150</field></shadow></value><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field></block>
          </next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block>
        </statement>
        <statement name="ELSE">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">12</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">7</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">6</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field></block>
          </next></block></next></block>
        </statement>
        <next>
        <block type="servo_write"><field name="PIN">9</field><value name="ANGLE"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">135</field></shadow></value><next>
        <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">400</field></shadow></value>
        </block></next></block>
        </next>
      </block>
      </next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a 🌈 NeoPixel 8x RGB Rainbow Audio Visualizer & Mood Lamp circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: Dynamic sound-and-light disco stage visualizer! An analog potentiometer connected to A0 acts as a tempo and color palette selector. The Arduino Uno translates this input into high-speed WS2812B digital bitstreams over D6, driving an 8-pixel RGB NeoPixel ring in continuous rainbow chase patterns synchronized with rhythmic audio beats pulsed on D8 buzzer.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">9600</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="neopixel_show"><field name="SENSOR">neo</field></block>
      </next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="neopixel_set_color"><field name="SENSOR">neo</field><value name="PIXEL"><block type="math_number"><field name="NUM">0</field></block></value><value name="COLOR"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">#ef4444</field></block></value><next>
      <block type="neopixel_set_color"><field name="SENSOR">neo</field><value name="PIXEL"><block type="math_number"><field name="NUM">1</field></block></value><value name="COLOR"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">#38bdf8</field></block></value><next>
      <block type="neopixel_show"><field name="SENSOR">neo</field><next>
      <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
      <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">150</field></shadow></value><next>
      <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
      <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">300</field></shadow></value>
      </block></next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a 📏 Ultrasonic Distance Sensor & 3-Zone Proximity Radar circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: Automotive 3-zone ultrasonic parking radar with acoustic frequency alarm! The HC-SR04 emits ultrasonic pings from Trig (D9) and Echo (D10) to calculate obstacle distance. Readings stream to Serial Monitor, while three zone LEDs (Green Safe on D13, Yellow Caution on D12, Red Hazard on D11) and Piezo Buzzer D8 provide instant visual and acoustic proximity warnings.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">9600</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">12</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">11</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field></block>
      </next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="serial_print"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">Target Distance: </field></block></value><next>
      <block type="serial_print"><value name="TEXT"><block type="ultrasonic_read"><field name="TRIG">9</field><field name="ECHO">10</field></block></value><next>
      <block type="serial_println"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT"> cm</field></block></value><next>
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0">
          <block type="logic_compare">
            <field name="OP">LT</field>
            <value name="A">
              <block type="ultrasonic_read"><field name="TRIG">9</field><field name="ECHO">10</field></block>
            </value>
            <value name="B">
              <block type="math_number"><field name="NUM">30</field></block>
            </value>
          </block>
        </value>
        <statement name="DO0">
          <block type="serial_println"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">⚠️ DANGER (<30cm): Sounding Alarm!</field></block></value><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">11</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">12</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field></block>
          </next></block></next></block></next></block>
          </next></block>
        </statement>
        <statement name="ELSE">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">11</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">12</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field></block>
          </next></block></next></block></next></block>
        </statement>
        <next>
          <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">400</field></shadow></value></block>
        </next>
      </block>
      </next></block></next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

target.explanation: Interactive digital decade counter! The Arduino Uno drives all seven segment bars (a-g on pins D2-D8) through common GND to render digits 0 through 9 with glowing LED precision. Each count transition triggers an audio chime on pin D10 and flashes the pulse LED on D13, while an on-canvas Pushbutton on D9 allows manual step increments.

instruction.text: Build a 🌡️ Climate Overheat Protection System circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: Analog thermal monitoring with automated cooling fan and dual status warnings! The TMP36 outputs linear voltage on A0. When temperature exceeds safe thresholds (30°C), Arduino activates the DC Motor Cooling Fan on D5, sounds the emergency audio siren on D8, and flips from Normal Green LED (D12) to Overheat Red LED (D13). ⚠️ Simulation abstraction only: the simulated D5→DC fan connection is not safe physical wiring. Never drive a real DC fan/motor directly from an Arduino GPIO. Use a correctly rated transistor/MOSFET or motor driver/relay, suitable motor power, common ground, and flyback-diode protection.

instruction.text: Build a ⛅ Digital Environmental Station circuit using Arduino Uno.

instruction.text: Build a 🏠 Automated Smart Home circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: High-voltage home automation with PIR motion and electromechanical relay! The PIR motion sensor monitors room occupancy on digital pin D7. When movement is detected, Arduino energizes an electromechanical relay module on pin D8. The relay's internal electromagnet closes the Normally Open (NO) contacts, routing power from a 9V battery to spin a ceiling cooling fan (DC motor) at 1800 RPM and illuminate the room lamp.
target.code: <xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml"><block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40"><statement name="SETUP"><block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">9600</field><next><block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">7</field><field name="MODE">INPUT</field><next><block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field></block></next></block></next></block></statement><statement name="LOOP"><block type="controls_if"><mutation else="1"></mutation><value name="IF0"><block type="pir_motion"><field name="SENSOR">pir</field></block></value><statement name="DO0"><block type="serial_print"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">🚶 Room Occupied: Switching Relay ON -> Cooling Fan & Lamp Active!</field></block></value><next><block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next><block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><block type="math_number"><field name="NUM">1200</field></block></value></block></next></block></next></block></statement><statement name="ELSE"><block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next><block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><block type="math_number"><field name="NUM">200</field></block></value></block></next></block></statement></block></statement></block></xml>

instruction.text: Build a ESP32 Mission 10 · Local HTTP Web Server & Phone Controller circuit using ESP32.

target.explanation: Launch an embedded HTTP Web Server on port 80 and switch Living Room and Bedroom LEDs from your Smartphone!
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="wifi_connect">
        <value name="SSID"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">SmartHome-WiFi</field></block></value>
        <value name="PASS"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">pixiu123</field></block></value>
        <next>
        <block type="wifi_server_begin">
          <field name="PORT">80</field>
          <next>
          <block type="wifi_server_on">
            <field name="PATH">/</field>
            <statement name="DO">
              <block type="wifi_server_send">
                <field name="STATUS">200</field>
                <field name="TYPE">text/html</field>
                <value name="CONTENT">
                  <block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT"><h1>🏠 Smart Home</h1><a href="/red/on">Turn ON Red</a><a href="/red/off">Turn OFF Red</a></field></block>
                </value>
              </block>
            </statement>
            <next>
            <block type="wifi_server_on">
              <field name="PATH">/red/on</field>
              <statement name="DO">
                <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">4</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
                <block type="wifi_server_send">
                  <field name="STATUS">200</field>
                  <field name="TYPE">text/html</field>
                  <value name="CONTENT">
                    <block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT"><h2>🔴 Red ON</h2><a href="/">Back</a></field></block>
                  </value>
                </block>
                </next></block>
              </statement>
            </block>
            </next></block>
          </block>
          </next></block>
        </next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">100</field></shadow></value></block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="wifi_connect">
        <value name="SSID"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">SmartHome-WiFi</field></block></value>
        <value name="PASS"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">pixiu123</field></block></value>
        <next>
        <block type="wifi_server_begin">
          <field name="PORT">80</field>
          <next>
          <block type="wifi_server_on">
            <field name="PATH">/</field>
            <statement name="DO">
              <block type="wifi_server_send">
                <field name="STATUS">200</field>
                <field name="TYPE">text/html</field>
                <value name="CONTENT">
                  <block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT"><h1>🏠 Smart Home</h1><a href="/red/on">Turn ON Red</a><a href="/red/off">Turn OFF Red</a></field></block>
                </value>
              </block>
            </statement>
            <next>
            <block type="wifi_server_on">
              <field name="PATH">/red/on</field>
              <statement name="DO">
                <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">4</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
                <block type="wifi_server_send">
                  <field name="STATUS">200</field>
                  <field name="TYPE">text/html</field>
                  <value name="CONTENT">
                    <block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT"><h2>🔴 Red ON</h2><a href="/">Back</a></field></block>
                  </value>
                </block>
                </next></block>
              </statement>
            </block>
            </next></block>
          </block>
          </next></block>
        </next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">100</field></shadow></value></block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a Pico Mission 3 · Button Toggle & Digital Input circuit using Raspberry Pi Pico.

target.explanation: Read a tactile pushbutton on Pico pin GP14 and turn an LED on GP15 on and off interactively.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">14</field><field name="MODE">INPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">15</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field></block>
      </next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0">
          <block type="io_digitalread"><field name="PIN">14</field></block>
        </value>
        <statement name="DO0">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">15</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field></block>
        </statement>
        <statement name="ELSE">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">15</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field></block>
        </statement>
      </block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

        </value>
        <statement name="DO0">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">4</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field></block>
        </statement>
        <statement name="ELSE">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">4</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field></block>
        </statement>
      </block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a Pico Mission 10 · Smart Agriculture & Relay Pump Automation circuit using Raspberry Pi Pico.

target.explanation: Monitor soil moisture on ADC1 (GP27) and automatically energize an electromechanical relay on GP13 when soil is dry.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0">
          <block type="logic_compare">
            <field name="OP">LT</field>
            <value name="A"><block type="soil_moisture_read"></block></value>
            <value name="B"><block type="math_number"><field name="NUM">400</field></block></value>
          </block>
        </value>
        <statement name="DO0">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field></block>
        </statement>
        <statement name="ELSE">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field></block>

instruction.text: Build a Mission 11 · MQ-2 Gas & Smoke Sentinel circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: Detect combustible gas or smoke PPM levels and activate emergency sound and warning strobe.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">9600</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field></block>
      </next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="serial_print"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">Gas PPM: </field></block></value><next>
      <block type="serial_println"><value name="TEXT"><block type="mq2_gas_read"><field name="SENSOR">gas</field></block></value><next>
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0">
          <block type="logic_compare">
            <field name="OP">GT</field>
            <value name="A"><block type="mq2_gas_read"><field name="SENSOR">gas</field></block></value>
            <value name="B"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">300</field></shadow></value>
          </block>
        </value>
        <statement name="DO0">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">200</field></shadow></value></block>
          </next></block></next></block>
        </statement>
        <statement name="ELSE">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">200</field></shadow></value></block>
          </next></block></next></block>
        </statement>
      </block>
      </next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a Mission 19 · AI Hand Gesture Smart Controller circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: Track hand gestures via AI Computer Vision (e.g. Thumbs Up) to command smart home servo and LED actuators without touching hardware.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">9600</field><next>
      <block type="ai_camera_enable"><field name="STATE">ON</field><next>
      <block type="servo_write"><field name="PIN">9</field><value name="ANGLE"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">0</field></shadow></value></block>
      </next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0">
          <block type="ai_is_gesture"><field name="GESTURE">thumbs_up</field></block>
        </value>
        <statement name="DO0">
          <block type="servo_write"><field name="PIN">9</field><value name="ANGLE"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">90</field></shadow></value><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">500</field></shadow></value></block>
          </next></block></next></block>
        </statement>
        <statement name="ELSE">
          <block type="servo_write"><field name="PIN">9</field><value name="ANGLE"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">0</field></shadow></value><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">200</field></shadow></value></block>
          </next></block></next></block>
        </statement>
      </block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a Mission 21 · AI Confidence Alarm circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: Turn AI confidence into a physical signal: when vision confidence passes your chosen threshold, light a warning LED.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="ai_camera_enable"><field name="STATE">ON</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field></block>
      </next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0"><block type="logic_compare"><field name="OP">GT</field>
          <value name="A"><block type="ai_confidence"></block></value>
          <value name="B"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">75</field></shadow></value>
        </block></value>
        <statement name="DO0"><block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field></statement>
        <statement name="ELSE"><block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field></statement>
      </block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a Mission 25 · AI Smart Doorbell circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: Detect a person, open a virtual door servo and sound an electronic doorbell using one AI-driven decision loop.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="ai_camera_enable"><field name="STATE">ON</field><next>
      <block type="servo_write"><field name="PIN">9</field><value name="ANGLE"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">0</field></shadow></value></block>
      </next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0"><block type="ai_is_detected"><field name="CLASS">person</field></block></value>
        <statement name="DO0">
